quick_english: Now the fourteenth chapter. The blessed Lord said: I will again declare the supreme, highest knowledge among knowledges, by knowing which all sages attained supreme siddhi. That very knowledge previously stated I will again speak with excellence, individually determining the nature of the gunas, in full detail. By 'having known which,' he declares the evident certainty and establishment of this knowledge.

For what is to be abandoned, once its cause is known, is easy — I, of unspeakable bliss-form, taking up my own expanding power as Brahman, my reflective power over beginningless atoms, set them transmigrating for grace.

quick_english: Know that tamas, born of ignorance, deludes all embodied beings and binds them through negligence, laziness, and sleep. O Bharata, even rare human birth, gained by long-accumulated merit and the one cause of liberation, is wasted by negligence. Thus it is said: one moment of life cannot be obtained with all jewels; he who leads it vainly is negligent and the lowest man. Laziness in auspicious deeds is complete sleep, and sleep is a despised state.

quick_english: When tamas increases, darkness, inertia, delusion, and confusion arise; when rajas increases, greed and related qualities arise gradually through all the senses.
When sattva increases, the embodied one goes to dissolution and attains pure worlds; through unbroken sattvic practice, increased sattva brings auspicious attainment.

quick_english: Seated like an indifferent one, not shaken by the strands, knowing they operate, the unwise stands and does not move.
Equal in pain and pleasure, in clod, stone, and gold, in pleasant and unpleasant, the steady one is equal in blame and self-praise.

He who is equal in honor and dishonor, friend and foe, abandoning fruits of all undertakings, is called beyond the strands; though appearing ignorant, he stands without discrimination, and from right knowing he does not fall from his own form.
